findings.claim_location: Section3.1 p3 Task4 necessity of dynamic interpretation; Section3.5 p5 metric; Section4.3 pp7-8 RQ3; AppendixC.4/D p16; Task4 notebook cells0,4,7
findings.assumptions: Valid reference-program unit tests, semantics-preserving compilation on relevant inputs, and quantitative final-label scoring; intended golden-data domain. No global execution validation of all164 reference programs is claimed.
findings.argument: Pinned notebook extracts assert lines directly from the canonical test field with no negative-label construction. Pinned JSONL has164 unique tasks and1140 selected assert lines, all cases nonempty. Under the stated oracle-validity premise every ground-truth assertion label is pass, so h(IR,assertion)=pass attains both assertion-level and all-correct task accuracy1 without inspecting IR. CPP/2, CPP/121 and CPP/149 sample assertions checked by independent semantic arithmetic.
findings.alternatives: Wrong answers on valid positive tests remain real errors; qualitative erroneous traces are preserved. A Boolean function returning false can occur within a true assertion. No claim models used the shortcut. Historical false oracle labels would require case-level evidence; invalid canonical tests require oracle audit.
findings.dependency: One of four core measurement tasks -> RQ3 execution-understanding interpretation and SC/IR attribution.
findings.impact: Task4 success scores cannot by themselves discriminate execution reasoning from label bias. Material core measurement damage, scoped to Task4; no invalidation of other tasks or fabricated-score claim.
findings.correction: Add verified false assertions/counterfactual programs, report balance/constant baseline and independently verify selected execution states. Balanced assertion labels limit constant accuracy to1/2, removing this shortcut only; new measurements needed.
